title: Compact Adopter Bootcamp — 3-Day Sprint Outline
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, repeatable 3-day bootcamp to take an engineering adopter from curiosity to a minimally instrumented production-ready SDK integration. The goal: low friction, measurable telemetry, and clear next-steps for productionization. Target audience: backend/frontend engineers integrating Redwood SDKs (JS/Python) in an app.

Notes to self (voice): keep it short, hands-on, avoid deep runtime internals. Emphasize common failure modes + quick fixes. Provide a checklist so eng advocates can run this in ~4 hours of facilitator time across 3 days.

High-level success criteria (how we measure):
- Participant can make a streaming generation call and receive structured responses in <15 minutes.
- Telemetry contract implemented (request_id + route + model + tokens) and events appear in our sandbox console.
- Basic retry/backoff and fallback-to-compat-model path implemented and tested.
- Integration smoke test in CI with one golden prompt.

Pre-reqs for participants:
- Laptop with Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, git, Docker (optional)
- Redwood dev API key (provisioned ahead of session)
- Repo clone link + minimal sample app (we'll hand out a repo with branches)

Day-by-day sprint outline:
Day 0 (pre-work, 15–30m):
- Share prework checklist: install tools, confirm API key, open repo.
- Quick video: 6min orientation — what the SDK does, where to look for logs.

Day 1 — Quickstarts & Happy Path (90–120m)
- 0–15m: Kickoff + objectives (facilitator)
  - Ask: "What are you building?" capture one line per team.
- 15–45m: Guided lab 1 — Hello generation (JS + Py snippets)
  - Create client, call generate/chat, receive response. Emphasize streaming toggle.
  - Walk through common errors: 401, malformed request, missing model param.
- 45–75m: Lab 2 — Structured output + function calling stub
  - Show how to request JSON schema/structured output and validate locally.
- 75–90m: Quick telemetry hookup (sandbox)
  - Add a minimal instrumentation call to send request_id + route + model to our sandbox endpoint. Confirm in console.
- 90–120m: Breakout: add to your sample app, push branch, open PR. Instructor reviews 1–2 PRs live.

Day 2 — Reliability Patterns & Cost Controls (90–120m)
- 0–20m: Short recap + common post-Day1 issues.
- 20–50m: Lab 3 — Retry/backoff & circuit breaker
  - Provide a small helper (ex: with exponential backoff, jitter). Show how to attach fallback to a cheaper/quantized model for latency bursts.
- 50–80m: Lab 4 — Batching and caching patterns (client-side caching + prefix caching outline)
  - Demo how to batch user messages with a debounce strategy; show token cost tradeoffs.
- 80–100m: Telemetry deep-dive: tag schema and sample dashboards
  - Confirm events from Day1 + Day2 appear; show per-route latency, cost-per-token. Add a simple alert rule for token spike.
- 100–120m: Breakout: add retry + telemetry assertion to CI test.

Day 3 — Observability, Rollout & Production Checklist (60–90m)
- 0–15m: Short recap + guardrail checklist review.
- 15–40m: Lab 5 — Canary rollouts & health probes
  - Add route-level rollout config; simulate an error and observe automatic fallback to canary policy.
- 40–60m: Lab 6 — Quality monitoring smoke test
  - Add one golden prompt set and a quick evaluator that asserts output coverage.
- 60–90m: Wrap + next steps
  - Assign production checklist (security review, KMS integration, retention policy, SLOs) and record action items.

Artifacts we ship with the bootcamp (repo layout):
- /starter-apps/minapp-js : minimal express + SDK usage
- /starter-apps/minapp-py : fastapi + SDK usage
- /scripts/telemetry-injector.js : small example to emit the telemetry contract
- /ci/golden-prompt-check.yml : smoke test in GitHub Actions
- /docs/checklists/production-onboarding.md : one-page checklist for security & infra

Telemetry contract (minimal):
- event_type: "sdk_request"
- payload keys required: request_id, team_tag, route, model_variant, num_tokens_total, status_code, latency_ms
- optional: user_id_hash, prompt_shard_id
- Implementation note: emit synchronously on success path, async fire-and-forget when appropriate. Ensure idempotency for retries.

Common pitfalls & facilitator tips:
- Participants copy-paste sample keys into prod — include clear "DO NOT USE IN PROD" banner in the starter repo and pre-provision ephemeral keys that expire in 48–72 hours.
- Streaming edge cases: larger responses may need client-side buffer tuning; demo how to stream resume from last good token in sample.
- Telemetry gaps: if console shows missing fields, verify request_id is generated by middleware and passed along context.
- Network flakiness: have a local mock server pattern to simulate 503s and rate limits.

Checklist for production handoff (one-liner items):
- Update API key to a managed secret (KMS/HSM)
- Add routing policy and low-cost fallback model in config
- Add token-budget alert and per-route alert rules
- Ensure golden-prompt CI is gated on merges to main
- Add SLO: 99th pctl latency < configured threshold for interactive routes

Open questions / backlog items (for follow-up sprints):
- Short generator: create a 30s explainer video for caching and batching tradeoffs (assigned: Marco)
- Template for legal/security checklist for Private deployments (blocked: security review)
- Lightweight SDK lint rule to prevent non-idempotent request bodies (investigate)
- Add a sandbox badge for repos that have telemetry wired and passing golden prompt CI

Facilitator playlist (materials & time budget):
- Prework email template (5m reading)
- 6min orientation video
- 3 lab notebooks (JS, Py, CI) — 45–60m each to complete during session
- 15m demo of console + metrics

Quick links for live run:
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/adopter-bootcamp-starters
- Sandbox console: https://console.redwood.dev/sandbox/projects/bootcamp-123
- Lab issue tracker: https://jira.company/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=42

Facilitator notes (final):
- Keep sessions interactive; prioritize participant apps. Aim to review at least one PR per team live.
- Log common issues into a running doc during the bootcamp; we’ll convert top-3 issues into FAQ snippets in the starter repo.
- After each cohort, capture anonymized telemetry summary to measure lift (time-to-first-success, telemetry wired %).

-- end --
